safety_verdicts.content: Headache is still present at the time of consultation.
safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: Gold states the headache is still present during the consultation; generated does not explicitly state ongoing presence at time of call.
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Failing to document that the headache was still ongoing at the time of the call reduces clarity about acuity and response to any self-care, which can affect reassessment/triage if symptoms worsen. The likely impact is limited to reduced clinical context and potential follow-up inefficiency rather than direct harm.

safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: Gold includes denial of neck stiffness; generated does not mention neck stiffness.
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Not recording denial of neck stiffness omits an important “red flag” negative for meningitis/SAH-type evaluations, which can complicate future triage decisions and safety-netting. This is more likely to cause unnecessary escalation or repeat questioning than direct patient injury.

safety_verdicts.content: Patient has no nausea at present.
safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: Gold includes no nausea at present; generated does not mention nausea.
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Omitting absence of nausea removes a key associated symptom used to differentiate migraine and other secondary headache causes and to guide antiemetic/analgesic choices. The harm is mainly loss of diagnostic/management precision and added reassessment burden.

safety_verdicts.content: Paracetamol taken by the patient did not relieve the headache.
safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: Gold states paracetamol did not help; generated only states paracetamol was taken, without effectiveness.
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Not documenting that paracetamol was ineffective can lead to suboptimal stepwise analgesia planning and may delay escalation to more effective therapy. The expected impact is mild (additional treatment steps/monitoring) rather than direct injury.
